svg.aria-label: How to write 解: 13 strokes · 12 pen lifts · 13 movements
svg.title: Writing 解
svg.desc: 13 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 解 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 解.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E8%A7%A3.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 解, in three pieces. Medians 1–7 draw 角 on the left: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, two short horizontals inside, then a vertical down the middle. Medians 8–9 draw the upper right: a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a left-falling stroke inside it. Medians 10–13 draw the lower right as 午 is written: a short left-falling stroke, two horizontals and a vertical through them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
